One sunny summer, in a nest by the pond, a mother duck sat on her eggs.
One by one the eggs cracked open, and out popped fluffy yellow ducklings.
But the biggest egg was still there.
At last the big egg cracked, and out came a big grey bird with a long neck.
Oh my,
said Mother Duck.
He does not look like my other babies.
But he swims very well, so he must be mine.
The other ducklings looked surprised.
You look different!
said Duckling's brothers.
Every day he felt a little more left out.
The ducks paddled off, the hens were busy, and nobody asked him to play.
Not today,
said Hen.
The little grey duckling felt sad.
One night he set off to look for friends, across the fields and over the marsh.
He wandered for a long time.
In the autumn the leaves turned brown and the wind grew cold.
He found a little cottage and went in, but a sleepy cat lived there.
Can you purr?
said Cat.
Can you catch mice?
No?
Then I think your home is somewhere else.
The winter was long and hard.
The duckling hid in the reeds by a frozen pond.
He was cold, and he missed having friends.
Will I ever find my family?
said Duckling.
But he did not give up, and slowly the snow melted.
At last it was spring.
The sun was warm and the birds were singing.
The duckling lifted his wings, and they were big and strong.
Whoosh!
He flew up into the air.
Below him, on a clear lake, floated three beautiful white swans.
I will fly down to them,
Perhaps they will not want to play, but I would like to say hello.
He bent his head to the water.
In the lake he saw not a grey bird, but a white swan with a long, graceful neck.
The three swans swam up to him.
Welcome, friend,
said Swan.
Come and swim with us.
I am not a plain grey bird after all,
said Duckling softly.
I was a swan all the time!
And the young swan spread his shining wings.
He was happier than he had ever dreamed.
